teaching.hint: After listing the primes in increasing order, which pairs could have the smallest gap?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: A nonadjacent prime pair contains at least one smaller consecutive gap, so only neighboring primes need comparison.
solution_outline.approach: Identify primes up to right once, scan those in the requested interval in increasing order, and retain the closest consecutive pair. Keep the first pair on equal gaps.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The previous seen prime and current best pair summarize every candidate gap seen so far; the best pair has minimum gap and earliest lower endpoint among ties.
solution_outline.correctness: Every possible optimum is adjacent in sorted prime order. The scan examines each adjacent pair once, and strict improvement preserves the required tie break.
solution_outline.complexity: O(right log log right) time and O(right) auxiliary space using a sieve up to right; the final scan is linear in the interval width.
solution_outline.pitfall: Treating 1 as prime or replacing the best pair on an equal gap violates the output rule.

common_wrong_turns: Break ties by the larger prime
source_fidelity_notes: The prime definition, inclusive bounds, no-pair output, and smallest-first tie rule are explicit.
